articles.title: Burundi: Humanitarian Action for Children 2026 - Protecting children amid overlapping crises in the Great Lakes, Revision 1 (November 2026)
articles.description: Please refer to the attached file. HIGHLIGHTS • In 2026, 6.1 million people, including children, will require urgent humanitarian assistance across Burundi, Rwanda, Uganda and the United Republic of Tanzania, as conflict spillover, displacement, climate shocks, malnutrition and disease outbreaks heighten risks to children’s survival, protection and well-being. • Persistent threats remain of public health outbreaks; through cross border transmission in a subregion marked by porous borders, high population mobility and fragile surveillance systems. In 2026, active Ebola transmission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda’s outbreak (officially declared over on 28 July), demonstrates these risks. Rising malnutrition, Cholera and other disease outbreaks are compounding risks for refugees and vulnerable host communities, where overstretched WASH, health and basic services require sustained preparedness, surveillance, regional coordination and life-saving support for children and affected communities. • UNICEF will scale up rapid, multisectoral life-saving assistance while reinforcing national systems to sustain access to essential services for both refugees and host communities. This integrated response will be anchored in community-based delivery, preparedness and early action and a coordinated cross-border response. UNICEF will work through local partners and government systems to maximize reach, timeliness and accountability. • UNICEF urgently requires $45 million to ensure more than 1.2 million children can access lifesaving treatment, safe water, protection and learning. Without sustained and flexible funding, the risks to children’s survival, well-being and rights will escalate sharply.
